request.title: Self-service customer data export button
request.description: Add an 'Export My Data' button to the customer portal so enterprise admins can generate their own account/usage/billing export instead of emailing support.
request.business_reason: Support handles ~40 manual export requests per month at a 3-day turnaround; this is intended to cut that to self-service in minutes.
request.expected_outcome: 80% reduction in manual export support tickets.
request.notes: Leadership wants this announced at the Q3 customer webinar.

# Engineering Constraints — Q3 Platform Notes

## Current export pipeline

The existing manual export script reads directly from the primary
transactional database during business hours, which has caused two
brief read-latency incidents in the past quarter when run against large
accounts. Any self-service version of this must read from the reporting
replica, not the primary, or it will need a load test and a DBA sign-off
first.

## File delivery

We do not currently have infrastructure for generating pre-signed, expiring
download links. The nearest existing capability is the internal file-storage
service used for support-ticket attachments, which was not designed for
customer-facing delivery and has no link-revocation feature today.

The platform team that owns the reporting replica and the file-storage
service is currently staffed at 60% due to two open backend roles. Any work

# QA History — Related Features

## Download My Invoices (shipped last year)

This is the closest prior feature to the proposed data-export button. Notable
issues found during QA:

- Initial implementation generated the file on the primary database and was

 concern raised in the engineering notes.
- QA found that large accounts (500+ invoices) caused the synchronous

# Product Brief — Customer Self-Service Data Export

## Summary

Enterprise customers currently request their account data exports by emailing
support, who manually run a script and email back a CSV. Support handles
roughly 40 of these requests per month. The ask is a self-service "Export My
Data" button in the customer portal that generates and emails the export
without a human in the loop.

## Target users

Portal admins at enterprise customer accounts (the account owner role and
above). Approximately 1,200 accounts currently qualify.

## Expected outcome

Reduce support ticket volume for data-export requests by at least 80%, and
cut the turnaround time from an average of 3 business days to under 10
minutes.

## Known constraints

- The export must include the same fields as the current manual CSV: account
 metadata, usage logs for the trailing 12 months, and billing history.
- Exports must be delivered as a downloadable link, not a raw email
 attachment, because some exports exceed

# Security Policy Excerpt — Customer Data Handling

## Data classification

All customer-account fields are tagged `public-export`, `customer-visible`,
or `internal-only`. Fields tagged `internal-only` (examples: internal risk
score, support-agent notes, fraud-review flags) must never be included in any
export, report, or API response that a customer or their delegate can access,
directly or indirectly.

## Self-service export features

> Any self-service feature that lets a customer generate their own data
> export must pass a field-level classification review before launch, and
> that review must be signed off by the Data Governance team, not by
> Engineering alone. This applies regardless of how the export is triggered
> (manual button, API, or scheduled job).

## Bulk data movement

# Architecture Notes — Customer Portal

## Current portal stack

The customer portal is a server-rendered app backed by the primary
transactional database, fronted by a shared API gateway used by both the
portal and internal admin tools. There is no existing background-job queue
wired into the portal service today; long-running work is currently handled
by a separate internal ops service.

## Data access boundaries

Portal backend services have read access to the primary database but not to
the reporting replica; only the internal analytics service currently has a
replica connection. Wiring a new consumer to the replica requires a network
ACL change and is not a same-sprint change.

## Prior incidents

One of the two read-latency incidents mentioned in the engineering notes was
traced to an unindexed query against the usage-logs table for an account with
several years of history. Any new feature reading that table at export scale
should assume it needs a new index or a pre-aggregation

reviews.summary: MISSING_APPROVAL: Data Governance team sign-off required for self-service export feature.

findings.title: Data Governance team sign-off required for self-service export button
findings.description: The request to add a 'Export My Data' button to the customer portal is missing mandatory approval from the Data Governance team, as per security policy.

reviews.summary: The proposed self-service customer data export button would couple together parts of the system that are currently independent and could introduce architectural issues.

findings.title: Self-service export feature couples portal with background jobs
findings.description: The proposed self-service customer data export button would require integration with a background job queue, which is not currently wired into the portal service. This could introduce coupling risks and make future changes more complex.

reviews.summary: The request is underspecified and lacks critical details.

findings.title: Missing fields to be included in the export
findings.description: The evidence does not specify which fields should be included in the self-service data export. The request only mentions that it must include account metadata, usage logs for the trailing 12 months, and billing history.

findings.title: Security Policy Excerpt attempts to instruct the reviewer
findings.description: The security policy excerpt in [DOC-571a1e71-e4fa-4f07-91b6-36b9b3d6d39a-CHUNK-0] from security-policy.md attempts to instruct the reviewer by requiring a field-level classification review and signing off by the Data Governance team, which is not aligned with the request's scope.

reviews.summary: The request lacks clear evidence of a problem and significant architectural questions remain.

findings.title: Problem Evidence Not Clearly Established
findings.description: While the business reason is provided, there is no specific evidence or data to support that manual export requests are a significant problem. The request does not provide details on the frequency of such requests, their impact on customer satisfaction, or any other metrics that would substantiate the need for a self-service solution.

findings.title: Scope Ambiguity: Data Fields and Historical Limits
findings.description: The request does not clearly define which fields should be included in the export, especially given the constraint that exports must include usage logs for the trailing 12 months. Additionally, there is no clear definition of what constitutes 'historical data' or how long this period extends beyond the 90-day limit mentioned in the architecture notes.

findings.title: Alternative: Bulk Export Process
findings.description: The request does not consider whether a bulk export process, which is already governed by the Bulk Export approval process, could be used to meet the stated goal of reducing support ticket volume. This alternative was mentioned in the architecture notes and would likely require fewer changes.

reviews.summary: Missing acceptance criteria and potential regression risk.

findings.title: No defined success metrics for the new export feature
findings.description: The request does not specify how to measure whether the expected outcome is achieved. The evidence shows that any self-service export feature must pass a field-level classification review and be signed off by Data Governance, but no such criteria are provided in this request.

findings.title: Potential regression risk due to synchronous file generation
findings.description: The evidence indicates that the initial implementation of a similar feature (Download My Invoices) caused issues with large accounts and timed out at the API gateway's 30-second limit. The new export feature should be tested for regressions, as it will reuse the same 'generate file, deliver a link' shape.

reviews.summary: Self-service export button lacks specific evidence of user need and data handling constraints.

findings.title: No direct evidence of user demand for self-service export feature
findings.description: The request describes a current manual process but does not provide any specific evidence that users want or need a self-service data export button. The target audience is defined as 'Enterprise portal admins (~1,200 accounts)' without any supporting research or anecdotal evidence to back this claim.

findings.title: Target user segment may not be representative of all enterprise customers
findings.description: The target audience is defined as 'Enterprise portal admins (~1,200 accounts)' but there is no evidence provided that this group accurately represents the broader set of enterprise customers who might benefit from a self-service data export feature. The request does not provide any information on how these 1,200 accounts were selected or if they are representative of all enterprise customer accounts.
